title: Tell your family and friends
whyMatters: How the people close to you react will color your first months as a Muslim more than almost anything else. A plan lets you choose what to say, keep yourself safe, and stop every conversation from turning into a debate.

exactActions.text: Decide who needs to know now
subSteps: Nobody says you have to tell everyone at once.
Start with the people who affect your safety, your housing, your food, your schedule, or your support.
If you expect someone to react badly, talk it through with a mentor first.
Tell them what Islam means to you rather than making a case for it.
Let the change show in how you treat them over time.
They may be afraid you are turning into a different person.
Some of what they think about Islam will have come from the news.
Answer gently, and say so when you do not know yet.
Stop a conversation that turns insulting or unsafe.
Stay in the relationship where you can, through kindness and small acts of help.
Ask for support if the pressure at home becomes controlling or threatening.

timeEstimate: About 30 minutes of planning before an important conversation

obstacles.problem: My family thinks I rejected them
obstacles.solution: Reassure them by being consistently kind. You can also explain that Islam holds you to good character and to keeping family ties, not cutting them.
You can say you are still learning and you would rather keep the peace between you. You are not obliged to answer every question the moment it is asked.

tinyVersion: Pick one safe person and get one calm sentence ready about why Islam matters to you.
unlocksNext: With steadier boundaries at home, community, learning, and daily practice all get easier to keep up.

contextNotes.title: Safety first
contextNotes.body: If telling someone could cost you your housing or put you at risk of harm or control, speak to a local support person you trust before you say anything.

gentleScripts.title: First conversation
gentleScripts.body: I want to tell you something important. I became Muslim because I believe in one God, and this has given me something I needed. I am still learning. I hope we can talk about it with respect.

gentleScripts.title: If it turns into an argument
gentleScripts.body: I love you and I do not want this to become a fight. Can we pause and come back to it another time?
